Put it in a **new migration file, `migrations/0008_add_customer_phone.sql`**. Don't edit `0007_add_customers.sql`.

The project's memory store has a rule that files in `migrations/` have already been applied in production. They must never be edited; every change gets a new file with the next 4-digit number. The newest one now is `0007`, so yours is `0008`:

```sql
ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN phone TEXT;
```

I made it nullable because existing customer rows have no phone number. If you need `NOT NULL`, you'll have to give it a default or backfill those rows first.

Separately, `0007_add_customers.sql` creates a column misspelled as `emial`, not `email`. If you want to fix that, it also has to be a new migration (`RENAME COLUMN`), not an edit to `0007`. You could do it in the same `0008` file or a separate one, and any code that reads that column would need updating too.

I haven't created the file. Say if you want me to.

Failing that, an `explain`/`debug` parameter on `query` showing why each candidate was dropped, so I could tell whether to retry with `path: "migrations/"` or `tags: ["migrations"]`. The `retrieval_quality: "full"` value hid the miss: it suggested the store had nothing relevant.

2. **Nothing surfaced at session start.** ENGRAM.md says to "expand surfaced memories" from session start, but the SessionStart hook only added a reflection reminder and no memories. I wanted the hook to include the hazard-type memories, or at least their titles and IDs; this store has only ten. Then the migration rule would have been in context without needing a query.

3. **No path-triggered surfacing.** I never opened or edited anything in `migrations/`, so no file-based scoping would have fired.
